comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C28-C36 regarding ATP-induced unfolding of Trp-cage. Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED, acknowledging increased radius of gyration, decreased contacts, and robust computational evidence across force fields.

Perfect agreement on claims C37-C43 regarding ATP-Trp-cage interaction mechanisms. Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED, acknowledging van der Waals interactions and protein-specific interaction patterns.

Perfect agreement on claims C45-C46, C48, C53, C56-C57 regarding ATP's effects on Aβ40. Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED, acknowledging expanded conformations, disruption of fibrillogenic motifs, and comprehensive computational metrics.

Perfect agreement on claims C54-C55, C94-C96 regarding protein-specific ATP interactions. Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED, explicitly acknowledging different interaction modes (van der Waals for Trp-cage vs. electrostatic for Aβ40) as a key strength.

Perfect agreement on claims C58-C60 regarding experimental validation of ATP dissolving preformed aggregates. Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED, treating ThT fluorescence and TEM imaging as key experimental strengths.

Strong agreement on claims C68-C72 regarding ATP's superiority over NaXS. Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. Peer review also includes C7 (broader claim about ATP superiority), while OpenEval focuses specifically on the comparative data.

Partial agreement on anti-aggregation mechanisms. Both address C61-C64 and find evidence SUPPORTED. Peer review also includes C65-C66 (disaggregation of preformed dimers), which OpenEval evaluates separately in R7.

Partial overlap on disaggregation claims C65-C66. OpenEval R7 finds these SUPPORTED as part of dissolving existing aggregates. Peer R6 groups these with anti-aggregation claims C61-C64, also finding them SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on overall mechanistic synthesis (C79-C81, C86-C87, C89-C90). Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. Peer review also includes high-level claims C4-C6, C8 about ATP's general solubilizing effects, treating the comprehensive mechanism as a key contribution.
Partial overlap on main conclusions. OpenEval R11 evaluates C4-C8 as SUPPORTED high-level findings. Peer R8 includes C4-C6, C8 as part of broader mechanistic evaluation, also finding them SUPPORTED.

Divergent evaluations despite shared claims C28-C32. OpenEval R1 finds Trp-cage unfolding evidence SUPPORTED. Peer R9 rates these claims UNCERTAIN due to concerns about unusually high ATP concentrations (1000-fold higher) used in simulations and whether mechanisms remain identical at physiological concentrations.

Divergent evaluations for overlapping claims C45-C46. OpenEval R3 finds Aβ40 conformational changes SUPPORTED. Peer R9 rates related claims UNCERTAIN due to concerns about high ATP concentrations affecting mechanism validity.

Divergent evaluations for overlapping claims C61-C62. OpenEval R6 finds anti-aggregation mechanisms SUPPORTED. Peer R9 rates related claims UNCERTAIN due to concerns about whether mechanisms at 1000-fold higher ATP concentrations reflect actual physiological processes.

Divergent evaluations for overlapping claim C65. OpenEval R7 finds disaggregation evidence SUPPORTED. Peer R9 rates related claims UNCERTAIN due to concerns about high ATP concentrations used in simulations.
